Operar las máquinas de acuerdo con las hojas de proceso, instrucciones de trabajo o cualquier otro requisito (especificaciones del cliente, planos de ingeniería, etc.). Verificar las piezas para comprobar que las medidas sean correctas y cumplan con las especificaciones. Realizar mantenimiento autónomo, cumpliendo con las instrucciones de la documentación TPM y de 5S. Utilizar la documentación de manufactura (hojas viajeras, primeros artículos de inspección, etc.) para fabricar productos que cumplan los requisitos de calidad; inspeccionar y verificar el trabajo antes de enviarlo a inspección y, si no es conforme, procesarlo según los procedimientos de material no conforme. Cumplir con los tiempos estándar y los horarios establecidos para el trabajo asignado. Notificar al supervisor sobre los problemas que surjan. Antes de inspeccionar las piezas, verificar que se utilicen instrumentos de medición bien calibrados y etiquetados, con fecha de calibración vigente por parte del departamento de metrología. Mantener las especificaciones observando que las herramientas de corte trabajen correctamente en las diferentes operaciones: taladros, ranuras, desbaste, acabado, etc. Mantener operaciones seguras cumpliendo con los procedimientos y regulaciones de seguridad. Mantener la continuidad entre turnos de trabajo documentando y comunicando acciones, irregularidades y necesidades en curso. Documentar las acciones, completando los registros de producción y calidad, ya sea en formato físico o en SAP. Actualizar los conocimientos de trabajo participando en capacitaciones. Cumplir los objetivos GE Aerospace aceptando los logros y solicitando nuevas necesidades/requerimientos. Seguir las normas o políticas de los organismos reguladores (AS, NADCAP o GE). Mantener un excelente historial laboral (por ejemplo: asistencia, actitud y productividad). Capacidad para usar y aplicar las fuerzas requeridas (por ejemplo: levantamiento de materiales de hasta 40 lb). review_candidates.description: What We Can Achieve Together The Content Strategy & Storytelling Manager is responsible for shaping and driving TNC Africa Region's content vision, editorial strategy, and storytelling agenda. This role serves as the primary architect of compelling narratives that showcase conservation impact, elevate partner and community voices, strengthen donor engagement, expand influence, and deepen audience connection with the organization's mission across Africa. This is a highly specialized content leadership position requiring exceptional editorial judgment, narrative development expertise, and demonstrated experience translating complex conservation, scientific, and community-based work into compelling stories that inspire action and support. Through exceptional writing, editing, interviewing, and production, this role will help TNC Africa demonstrate conservation impact and deepen connections with strategic stakeholders and audiences. The position leads the development of strategic content plans and manages the end-to-end storytelling process, from story identification and field reporting to writing, editing, multimedia production, publishing, and performance analysis. The role collaborates closely with conservation, policy, philanthropy, and Marketing and Communications experts, both regionally and globally, to ensure content aligns with organizational priorities and engages audiences through powerful, authentic, and evidence-based storytelling. In partnership with creative agencies, photographers, and videographers, the incumbent will identify, develop, produce, and publish high-quality storytelling assets. Nature.org will be the primary delivery platform, complemented by video productions, blogs, podcasts, photo stories, and other creative multimedia formats. The role reports to the Director Marketing & Communications - Africa and shall be based in any country where TNC has offices, in Kenya, Tanzania, Gabon, Zambia, South Africa, Angola. No employment visas or assistance is being offered with this position except for the local labour employment requirements. We’re Looking For You Are you a strong writer, editor, producer, and creative storyteller who can transform complex conservation science into clear and memorable content? Are you excited by the opportunity to report from some of Africa’s irreplaceable landscapes, work with partners, communities, and conservation teams, create donor-focused stories, and help expand influence in written, visual, video, and audio formats? We are looking for someone with excellent editorial judgment, a strong portfolio, and the ability to manage content from initial idea through publication. By joining the Africa Marketing and Communications team, you will help bring our Big 5 Irreplaceable Landscapes story to life and connect donors with the people, places, and conservation outcomes their support makes possible. Role Scope & Key responsibilities Content Strategy & Editorial Leadership Develop and own the Africa content and storytelling strategy aligned with regional priorities, conservation objectives, philanthropic engagement goals, and organizational brand standards. Establish an editorial vision and annual storytelling roadmap that identifies priority themes, narratives, audiences, and content opportunities across Africa. Lead content planning processes to ensure a consistent pipeline of high-impact stories throughout the year. Define storytelling frameworks, editorial standards, voice, tone, and content governance practices. Advise leadership and program teams on strategic storytelling approaches that strengthen audience engagement and showcase impact. Identify emerging stories, trends, and content opportunities that support regional priorities and strategic objectives. Story Development & Narrative Creation Serve as the lead storyteller, writer, and editor for the Africa region. Identify, source, research, and develop compelling stories from landscapes, communities, Indigenous Peoples, conservation practitioners, scientists, donors, partners, and staff. Transform complex scientific, technical, and conservation information into clear, engaging, audience-centered narratives. Produce feature stories, long-form articles, case studies, donor stories, scripts, blogs, and impact reports. Conduct interviews and gather firsthand information to build authentic, evidence-based narratives. Ensure all content reflects diverse voices, local perspectives, and ethical storytelling practices. Multimedia Storytelling & Content Production Lead the conception and development of multimedia storytelling projects, including video, photography, audio, and digital content. Travel to field sites to conduct reporting, interviews, story gathering, and content production activities. Develop creative briefs and storytelling concepts for visual and multimedia projects. Collaborate with photographers, videographers, designers, editors, and production partners to produce high-quality storytelling assets. Oversee content production workflows and ensure consistency with editorial and storytelling objectives. Maintain a library of approved stories, photographs, video assets, and supporting content resources. Audience Engagement & Content Performance Monitor content effectiveness using audience insights, analytics, and engagement metrics. Evaluate storytelling performance across channels and recommend improvements based on data and audience behavior. Apply audience research and engagement data to strengthen narrative approaches and content decisions. Measure the effectiveness of storytelling initiatives in supporting donor engagement, partnership development, and organizational visibility. Content Collaboration & Internal Consulting Partner with philanthropy, conservation, science, policy, country, and digital teams to identify strategic storytelling opportunities. Provide editorial guidance and storytelling support to colleagues across the Africa region. Review, edit, and strengthen content created by internal contributors and external partners. Serve as a subject matter expert on storytelling best practices and content development. Building the network and collaborations to ensure Africa stories are elevated for global showcases. Exceptional writing, editing, interviewing, and narrative development skills. Demonstrated experience developing content strategies and managing editorial pipelines. Experience producing content across multiple formats, including written, digital, visual, and multimedia platforms. DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor’s degree in journalism, Communications, Media Studies, English, or related field. 8+ years of professional experience in content strategy, editorial leadership, journalism, storytelling, publishing, or multimedia content development. Experience working in conservation, environmental, development, sustainability, or nonprofit sectors. Background in journalism, documentary storytelling, or editorial publishing. Experience producing stories for donor, philanthropic, and partnership audiences. Knowledge of digital content performance metrics and audience engagement strategies. Experience working across multiple African countries and cultures. Strong understanding of ethical storytelling, representation, and inclusive narrative practices. Strong portfolio demonstrating impactful storytelling and editorial leadership. Experience gathering stories through direct field reporting and stakeholder interviews. Excellent project management skills with experience managing multiple content initiatives simultaneously. Excellent relationship-building and collaboration skills, with experience working across cultures, functions, locations, and time zones. Fluency in written and spoken English.
